The navigation-stability question ("is there persistent navigation?") is already **answered with real pixel measurements** — `/imagine/paging/navigation/` tested rail, reserved-height, reserved-tabs, and full-screen-rail mechanisms and recorded exactly how many px each one moves. 5. `/imagine/paging/templates/` (11 real page shapes) plus `/imagine/paging/make/` (the one editor that saves a page's layout words to its own `page.json`) is the closest existing thing to the "create a new page, pick its shape" system the owner wants — likely the base to extend.

Five biggest finds:

1. **`page.jsonl` has no monitor or purge — 480 files, largest 257 KB — and it's already causing shared-worktree commit collisions today.** This is exactly what the brief asked about, and it's live and unresolved.
2. **The owner already decided the "swapping vs switching" navigation question**: "stable" (nothing you're reading moves) vs "dynamic" navigation, proven at 0px drift with 4 demos, plus a shipped core fix so an open column never resizes when a sibling opens.

## Done — commit `8f173f3773ec6e8912b878dc8112c40eff361d10` on `worktree/page-system-929`

**1. `create_page` does the whole mechanical job** ✅
Now requires `description`, writes it into line 1, writes a `readme.md` stub (Index/Use/Watch out/More headings), skips creating an empty `doc/`, and returns the parent's title, layout words (`layout`/`cols`/`room`), sibling names and readme url. Output pasted above — success path, both stub files, no `doc/`, the teaching error, and clean cleanup.

**2. `Server/page-size.mjs`** ✅
Report only, always exits 0. Run against the main tree: **484 `page.jsonl` files, 1 over 100 KB** — `ai/2026/09/24/prompt-mechanics-2/chat-as-right-hand-column/page.jsonl`, 252 KB, 21 lines (output pasted above, both plain and `--json`).

**3. `core/Page/doc/page-jsonl.md`** ✅ (new)
Source-of-truth summary (links `doc/jsonl.md` for the format detail so it's not duplicated), today's numbers from #2, the live-server-write commit-collision friction (confirmed live while I worked — see below), and a purge proposal (fold old lines into a `{"snapshot": …}` line, move raw lines to `page.<date>.jsonl`, trade-off named).
⚠️ Not yet linked from `core/Page/page.js`'s `notes:` — that file is outside my fence (per the brief, `core/Page` readme/page.js belongs to module-experts / the parent task). Until it's added there, the page resolves fine at `/framework/core/Page/doc/page-jsonl/` but logs one console 404, same as any unregistered doc. Flagging for whoever wires step 7 of the parent task.

**4. Skills, all kept at or under their prior length** ✅
- `new-page` (62 lines, was 62): leads with "call `create_page`", keeps only the traps it *can't* cover.
- `page` (117 lines, was 117): step 2 gets "a child starts from its parent — read what `create_page` hands back first."
- `documentation` (74 lines, was 75): one sentence — readme is the text version, the page is the navigational version designed FROM it, short-term duplication is fine, links the (not-yet-landed) `core/Page/make/readme-page/` example.

**5. Traps removed from `new-page` and why:**
- The whole "How an agent makes a page" bottom section, folded into step 2 — it was redundant with the new create_page-first instruction.
- The old step 3's framing as a *hand* step ("add its name to the parent's `children:`") — `create_page` now does this reliably; kept only the sub-traps that still bite when someone edits `children:`/`icon:` by hand anyway (routable-vs-linked, hand-declared-before-built 404, blog's undeclared posts, icon glyph validity) — those aren't mechanical steps `create_page` performs, they're judgment about what you write, so they stay.

**Proof:** `node --check Servex/pages.js` and `node --check Server/page-size.mjs` both pass. No spawns, so no `windowsHide` needed. Servex not restarted. Didn't touch `core/Page/navigation/` (the other minion's files). Budget: well under $3.
